verdict.rationale: Termius documents a Keychain whose items 'can be referenced by multiple Hosts and Groups without duplicating them,' and it stores credentials and keys in end-to-end encrypted vaults synced across devices. Community comments express general wariness about storing credentials in a third-party app, but none concretely contradicts the capability. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of credential reuse across hosts, and deeper documentation of how referencing and updating shared identities works.

support.subject: As a developer, I can store credentials once in a secure vault and reference them from multiple hosts

citations.quote: Items in the Keychain can be referenced by multiple Hosts and Groups without duplicating them.
Vaults in Termius are the end-to-end encrypted cloud storage for Hosts, Keys, Snippets, Port Forwarding rules, and Known Hosts.
Vaults serve as a single source of truth for Hosts, Groups, Snippets, Port Forwarding rules, and Credentials, which are stored securely and updated in real time.
